Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Consumer Brands Inc., or GCB as many of you know us, Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to register by pressing star one one on your telephone keypad followed by your name and affiliation. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss GCB's Q3 2024 results. With me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Hargrove, Chief Financial Officer; Raj Singh, Chief Marketing Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. GCB delivered a solid Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.

Our discussion today will cover five key aspects: overall financial performance, brand performance and innovation, supply chain and operational efficiency, marketing and promotional activities, and outlook for the remainder of the year.

I will now turn the call over to Lisa Hargrove to provide more detail on our financial results.

Lisa Hargrove:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $2.54 billion, representing a 6% increase compared to the prior year. Gross margin was 51.8%, driven by pricing discipline, supply chain efficiencies, and productivity gains. Operating income was $463 million, up 12% year-over-year. Diluted earnings per share were $1.32. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives.

Let me dive deeper into our financial results, starting with gross margin performance. Our gross margin percentage came in at 51.8% for the quarter—up 220 basis points year-over-year from 49.6% in Q3 2023, and 80 basis points sequentially from Q2's 51.0%. This marks our sixth consecutive quarter of gross margin expansion, a testament to the resilience of our CPG portfolio amid persistent input cost headwinds and a dynamic macroeconomic environment. For context, our trailing 12-month gross margin now stands at a robust 51.2%, positioning us at the higher end of our peer set, comparable to leaders like Procter & Gamble and ahead of Unilever's recent averages.

Gross margin is the foundational metric for our operating leverage in the consumer goods space, where COGS—dominated by commodities, packaging, and freight—can swing dramatically with global supply dynamics. Let me break this down driver-by-driver.

First, the positives, which accounted for roughly 350 basis points of expansion. Pricing discipline and mix shift contributed 140 basis points. We executed targeted pricing actions across 70% of our portfolio, capturing an average unit retail increase of 7.2%, in line with category inflation but ahead of private label growth. This was particularly effective in North America, where premiumization drove a 2.5-point favorable mix shift—think our Everyday Essentials brand's transition to high-margin sustainable packaging variants, like the 15% market share grab in plant-based snacks, echoing the success we've seen with Beyond Meat partnerships but fully owned in-house. In contrast, Europe saw more muted pricing at 5.8% due to regulatory scrutiny on shrinkflation, but our velocity on core SKUs like fabric care remained top-quartile.

Supply chain efficiencies and procurement savings added 120 basis points. Our CPG Agile Supply initiative, now fully rolled out across 85% of our 120 global plants, delivered $180 million in quarterly savings—think AI-optimized inventory turns, now at 8.2x versus 7.1x last year, and robotic process automation reducing direct labor in bottling lines by 12%. We locked in forward contracts for 60% of our palm oil needs at $950 per metric ton, well below the spot price spike to $1,200 per metric ton driven by El Niño weather patterns in Southeast Asia. Cocoa, a pain point for peers like Hershey and Mondelez, pressured our confectionery segment by 50 basis points, but our diversified sourcing from West Africa—blending Ivory Coast futures at $4,200 per metric ton with Ghana spot—mitigated this to a net neutral.

Productivity and footprint optimization contributed 90 basis points. SKU rationalization culled 1,200 low-velocity items, boosting gross margin by streamlining our 15,000-SKU portfolio toward high-margin heroes like our Zero Sugar beverage line, which grew 18% tonnage. Facility consolidations in Latin America, including the recent Mexico plant upgrade with energy-efficient dryers, cut conversion costs by 8% per case.

Now, the headwinds, which shaved off about 130 basis points. Input cost inflation dragged 80 basis points. Dairy proteins rose 11% year-over-year due to EU supply constraints from avian flu outbreaks, hitting our yogurt and nutrition bars. Freight out, up 6% on ocean rates amid Red Sea disruptions, added 30 basis points—though our nearshoring to U.S. Midwest hubs for North American distribution kept this contained versus peers reliant on transpacific routes.

FX and regional mix added a 50 basis point drag. Adverse FX in emerging markets, particularly a 15% devaluation in Argentina, pressured reported margins in our LatAm segment, where inflation-adjusted pricing lagged at 4.5%.

Regionally, North America delivered 53.4% margins—our strongest ever—fueled by e-commerce penetration at 22% of sales and premium adult beverages like our Hard Seltzer line outpacing Bud Light's category recovery. Europe held steady at 49.2%, resilient despite 2% volume softness from consumer downtrading amid 8% energy inflation, bolstered by our laundry pods competing head-on with Persil. Asia-Pacific shone at 52.1%, with Indonesia and India driving tonnage growth in personal care via affordable sachets, though competition from local players like Patanjali squeezed promotional spend. Emerging markets overall contributed a 1.8-point mix tailwind from higher-margin health and wellness.

Strategically, this isn't a one-off; it's embedded in our Margin Momentum 2026 playbook. We're investing $500 million over the next two years in regenerative agriculture—partnering with suppliers like Cargill for traceable soy—to hedge commodity volatility and appeal to Gen Z's sustainability premiums, potentially adding 100-150 basis points long-term. Portfolio reshaping continues: we divested low-margin pet food last quarter for $300 million, recycling into R&D for functional foods akin to Nestlé's Vital Pursuit. And our digital twin supply chain modeling, powered by SAP and AWS, forecasts 200 basis points more expansion by fiscal 2026.

Looking forward, we guide Q4 gross margins to 52.0-52.5%, with full-year at 51.5%—about 250 basis points above prior year—assuming stable FX and commodity curves. Risks remain around cocoa's $5,000 per metric ton potential peak and U.S. port strikes, but our $2 billion cost savings pipeline gives us ample buffer.

Moving on to our advertising and promotion, or A&P, investments and the strong returns they're delivering. In the CPG space, where margins are tight and shelf space is a battleground, disciplined A&P allocation is our growth engine. We're not just spending; we're engineering ROI through data-driven precision.

For Q3, total A&P spend came in at $285 million, up 8% year-over-year, representing 11.2% of net sales. This is right in line with our full-year target of 11-12% of sales, reflecting a deliberate ramp-up in a high-inflation environment where consumers are trading down but still rewarding premium innovation. Breaking it down further: advertising spend—think TV, digital, and out-of-home—was $145 million, or 51% of total A&P, up 12% year-over-year as we leaned into brand-building amid softening category growth. Promotion spend, including trade allowances, shopper marketing, and coupons, hit $140 million, up 4% year-over-year but flat as a percentage of sales at 5.5%, thanks to smarter negotiation with key retailers like Walmart and Kroger.

Now, the real story is ROI. Our return on marketing investment, or ROMI, averaged 4.2x across the portfolio for Q3, up from 3.8x a year ago and beating our internal hurdle of 3.5x. This translates to $1.20 in incremental sales for every A&P dollar deployed—a testament to our shift toward performance channels. Payback period shortened to 9 months from 11 months year-over-year, driven by quicker velocity on high-margin SKUs like our revamped NutriFresh protein bars and EcoClean laundry pods, which saw 15% market share gains in IRI scan data.

Unpacking the trends fueling this: media mix evolution shows digital now accounts for 45% of our ad budget, up from 32% in Q3 2023, with connected TV and social video growing 25% year-over-year. Traditional linear TV still holds 30% for mass reach on household staples, but we're optimizing GRPs down 5% while lifting effective frequency via addressable tech. In promotions, we're seeing trade spend efficiency improve 18% through retailer media networks—Walmart Connect and Target Roundel delivered 5.8x ROMI on sponsored search for our snack lines, outpacing off-platform coupons.

On the technical front, we're leveraging AI at scale. Our proprietary Shopper Genome platform, powered by first-party data from loyalty programs with Albertsons and Publix, uses machine learning to predict purchase propensity with 92% accuracy. This enabled hyper-targeted campaigns: for instance, geofenced digital out-of-home ads around 1,200+ Dollar General stores drove a 22% uplift in basket incidence for our value-pack yogurts. We're also piloting clean-room tech with The Trade Desk and Amazon DSP to activate anonymized second-party data, blending it with Nielsen panel lift studies for causal ROMI measurement. Early results? A 28% ROMI boost on our beauty segment, rivaling Unilever's precision playbook.

Regionally, performance varied but trended positive. In North America, our core market at 65% of A&P, spend rose 10% to $185 million, with ROMI at 4.6x—strongest in snacks and beverages, where Amazon Advertising's video format crushed it at 6.2x amid e-commerce's 28% penetration growth. Europe, 20% of spend at $57 million, faced headwinds from GDPR tightening and inflation-weary shoppers; ROMI here was 3.4x, flat year-over-year, but we're countering with localized content on TikTok Shop in the UK and Germany, targeting Gen Z for our plant-based dairy alternatives. APAC and LATAM, combining for 15% at $43 million, shone brightest with 5.1x ROMI—Tmall and Shopee live-streaming for our instant noodles in China delivered 7x returns, offsetting softer in-store promo ROI in Brazil due to FX volatility.

Strategically, we're pruning low-ROI tactics: cut 15% of slotting allowances on underperformers, redirecting to hero brands like EcoClean, which now commands 18% ACV in mass channels per Circana. We're also embedding zero-based budgeting with marketing mix modeling refreshed quarterly, factoring in halo effects from P&G-style influencer ecosystems—our 50+ creator partnerships generated $45 million in earned media value at near-zero cost. Amid broader industry dynamics—category slowdowns at -1% ex-soap, per Kantar—this A&P rigor helped us outpace peers, gaining 120 basis points in dollar share.

Looking forward, Q4 A&P guidance is $290-300 million, or 11.5% of sales, with digital mix hitting 50%. We'll accelerate retail media to 25% of budget, targeting 4.5x blended ROMI, and launch GenAI creative tools to cut production costs 20%. Risks? Rising CPMs on Meta and Google, but our walled-garden focus mitigates that.

Now, let's turn to our performance across key categories and brands, where we delivered a balanced set of results amid a dynamic macroeconomic environment. Our portfolio is anchored in four core pillars—Beverages, Snacks, Beauty & Personal Care, and Household Essentials—spanning powerhouse brands that generated over 85% of our fiscal 2023 net sales. In Q3, category net sales grew 6% as reported, or 4% organically, outpacing the global CPG industry average of 2% per NielsenIQ global scans. This reflects disciplined pricing actions averaging 7% across the portfolio, targeted innovation, and share gains in 12 of our top 15 markets via IRI and Kantar distribution metrics.

Beverages saw 8% organic growth, our brightest spot. Our Beverages segment, led by Zest Cola—our $4.2 billion flagship carbonated soft drink—and Power Surge energy drinks, posted standout results with volume up 2% and pricing up 6%. Zest Cola gained 110 basis points of U.S. market share to 28.5% in the CSD category, driven by our Zest Zero low-sugar reformulation, which captured 15% of incremental volume per Circana data. Power Surge surged 22% organically, fueled by functional hydration extensions like Power Surge +Electrolytes, tapping into the $12 billion global energy drink market growing at 7% CAGR.

Regionally, North America drove 60% of growth with e-commerce velocity up 25% on platforms like Amazon and Instacart, while Europe saw +5% amid cooler weather headwinds offset by our sustainability-linked packaging switch to 100% rPET, boosting retailer support from Tesco and Carrefour. In emerging markets, Latin America volumes grew 12% on affordable sachet packs in Brazil and Mexico, where inflation-adjusted pricing held firm at +9%. Strategically, we're accelerating premiumization—expect 20% of innovation pipeline to focus on functional beverages like adaptogen-infused RTDs—while our Route-to-Market tech initiative, leveraging AI-optimized DSD routing, delivered $25 million in logistics savings year-to-date.

Snacks achieved 3% organic growth, resilient amid salty snack slowdown. Snacks, powered by Crunchy Bites tortilla chips ($2.8 billion brand) and our fast-growing NutriBar protein snacks, grew steadily despite a 1% category contraction per Euromonitor. Pricing rose 8% to combat input cost inflation—commodity oils up 15% year-over-year—while volumes held flat through trade spend optimization, reducing A&P as a percent of sales by 50 basis points to 12%. Crunchy Bites added 80 basis points U.S. share to 22%, propelled by limited-time Spicy Lava flavor that trended #1 on TikTok SnackTok, driving 18% impulse buy uplift at checkout per IRI. NutriBar exploded +35%, riding the health halo with 15g plant-based protein variants, capturing share from KIND and RXBAR in the $6 billion bar segment.

Asia-Pacific was the hero here, up 10% organically on premium air-fried launches in China via Tmall, where we gained 2 points distribution to 45%. Challenges persisted in EMEA, with -2% volumes from private label aggression at Aldi and Lidl, prompting our Shopper Mission analytics platform to refine assortment—resulting in 300 SKUs delisted for better velocity. Looking ahead, we're investing $150 million in regenerative agriculture for nut sourcing, targeting ESG premiums and cost stability as cocoa and palm prices remain volatile.

Beauty & Personal Care posted 5% organic growth, e-commerce fueled. This high-margin segment, headlined by GlowEssence skincare ($1.9 billion) and FreshWave shampoos, benefited from at-home indulgence trends, with DTC sales up 30% via our GlowHub app and Ulta partnerships. Organic growth reflected 4% volume expansion and 1% pricing, with GlowEssence's Bio-Retinol serum line—clinically proven for 2x faster wrinkle reduction—driving 25% category growth and 150 basis points share gains versus L'Oréal and Estée Lauder. FreshWave held 18% U.S. mass-market share, bolstered by clean beauty claims amid regulatory tailwinds like the EU's Green Claims Directive.

Regionally, North America led at +7%, with prestige bleed-in from Sephora trials, while India and Southeast Asia volumes popped 15% on affordable GlowEssence Lite sachets, navigating +12% FX headwinds. Productivity from our Precision Fermentation tech—scaling biotech actives—shaved 3% from COGS, funding expanded trials in microbiome-focused haircare. Strategically, we're pruning low-velocity legacy SKUs (5% of portfolio) to fuel M&A in K-beauty, eyeing tuck-ins like a Drunk Elephant equivalent for $200-300 million.

Household Essentials was flat organically, in stabilization mode. Household, anchored by CleanSweep laundry detergents and Sparkle wipes ($3.1 billion combined), faced headwinds from deflationary pricing pressures and inventory destocking, posting flat organic with volumes down 3% but pricing up 3%. CleanSweep maintained 24% U.S. share per Nielsen, with our enzyme-boosted Ultra-Concentrate pods gaining 10% distribution at Walmart and Target, countering P&G's Tide Pods dominance. Sparkle disinfecting wipes grew 12% post-pandemic, riding hygiene rebounds.

EMEA dragged at -4% from energy crisis-driven downtrading, but LatAm rebounded +6% on value packs in Argentina amid 200% inflation. Our SmartFill subscription model—now 2 million U.S. households—lifted retention 15% via predictive replenishment AI. Forward, $100 million in capex for North American hypoallergenic expansions targets the $15 billion sensitive-skin subsegment growing 9% CAGR.

Cross-category, health & wellness now 35% of sales (up from 28% last year), with premium SKUs outperforming value by 2x. Share gains totaled 90 basis points globally, per our Kantar Worldpanel tracking, via 1,200 basis points of shelf resets won year-to-date. Supply chain resilience shone—inventory days down to 45 from 52—despite Red Sea disruptions adding $10 million in ocean freight. We're on track for $400 million in gross productivity savings for FY24, reinvested 60/40 into innovation and brand building.

In summary, our categories demonstrate the strength of our Own the Moment strategy—premiumize, digitize, and localize—positioning us to gain share in a 3-4% industry growing to $6 trillion by 2028 per McKinsey. We remain confident in our FY24 organic sales guide of 4-6% and margin expansion of 100-150 basis points.

I will now turn the call over to Raj Singh to discuss marketing and brand performance.

Raj Singh:
Thank you, Lisa. We saw strong performance in our Zest Cola and Crunchy Bites brands this quarter. Before we open the line for questions, I'd like to provide a detailed update on our new product launches and innovation pipeline—a key driver of our top-line growth and a testament to our commitment to category leadership in the CPG space. As you know, innovation has been the cornerstone of our strategy, accounting for 22% of our net sales over the past three years, well above the industry average of 15% as reported by NielsenIQ. In Q3 alone, new products—defined as items launched within the last 24 months—delivered $285 million in incremental revenue, representing 18% of total segment sales and up 14% year-over-year.

Our recent launches have exceeded our internal velocity targets and are gaining strong distribution traction. Our standout performer has been the VitaBloom Plant-Powered Protein Bars, launched in North America in late Q2. Formulated with upcycled pea protein and adaptogens like ashwagandha for stress relief—a nod to the booming functional wellness trend—these bars achieved 2.5x category velocity in the first 12 weeks, selling over 1.2 million units at an average retail price of $2.49. IRI data shows we've captured 8.2% NMV share in the $4.2 billion protein bar segment, outpacing competitors like Clif and RXBAR. Household penetration has hit 4.1% in test markets, with repeat purchase rates at 28%—driven by our clean-label positioning (no artificial sweeteners, 10g fiber per bar) amid consumer shifts toward gut health post-pandemic.

Internationally, AquaPure+, our zero-calorie, electrolyte-infused sparkling water with embedded vitamins, has been a game-changer in EMEA. Launched across the UK, Germany, and France in early Q3, it posted €45 million in Q3 sales, fueled by a 35% distribution gain to 65% ACV in grocery channels. Sustainability was key here: our proprietary algae-derived electrolytes reduce water usage by 40% in production compared to traditional sports drinks, aligning with EU Green Deal mandates. We've seen 22% trial rates in Kantar panels, with premium pricing at €1.79 per 500ml bottle holding firm despite inflationary pressures.

In APAC, particularly China and India, GlowEssence Skincare Essentials—our K-beauty inspired, hyaluronic acid-infused facial mists with probiotic ferments—launched via e-commerce partners like Tmall and Flipkart. These generated $52 million in sales, with 45% coming from DTC channels. Market share in the $12 billion facial mist subcategory grew to 6.7%, thanks to TikTok virality and influencer partnerships, which drove 1.8 million units in the first month alone.

Turning to our innovation pipeline, we're operating from a position of strength with a robust 150+ SKUs in the funnel—up 20% from last year—supported by $420 million in FY23 R&D investment, or 3.2% of sales, in line with peers like Unilever and P&G. Our pipeline is segmented across stages: 25% in discovery, 40% in development, and 35% in commercialization/readiness.

Key technical initiatives underscoring this include our AI-Accelerated Formulation Lab in Cincinnati, leveraging machine learning models trained on 50,000+ historical recipes to cut development time from 18 to 9 months. For instance, this tech powered NutriForge Meal Replacements, our upcoming keto-friendly shakes with precision-fermented proteins—launching Q4 in the US. Early consumer testing via our 10,000-panel InsightEdge network shows 85% purchase intent, targeting the $8 billion meal replacement market where we're aiming for 5% share by FY25.

Sustainability remains non-negotiable: 70% of our pipeline incorporates mono-material rPET packaging, reducing virgin plastic by 60% and enabling 95% recyclability. A prime example is EcoBrew Cold Brew Coffee Pods, set for North America and LatAm in Q1 FY25. Using mycelium-based composites for pod casings—in partnership with biotech firm MycoWorks—these dissolve in hot water, addressing Keurig-style pod waste concerns. Pilot runs project $180 million in Year 1 sales, capitalizing on the 12% CAGR in ready-to-drink coffee.

Regionally, we're tailoring to local dynamics. In North America, health & wellness dominates—65% of pipeline—with low-sugar, high-protein innovations responding to GLP-1 drug trends like Ozempic, which we estimate will shrink impulse snacking by 7-10% per Circana. EMEA focuses on premiumization and regulatory compliance, with 40% of launches featuring EU Organic certification; our HerbVitality Tea Line (adaptogen-infused, launching Q4) targets the €2.5 billion RTD tea segment, where inflation has boosted value-perceived premium packs.

In APAC, e-commerce and personalization rule: 55% of India/China pipeline is DTC-first, using genetic personalization tech via our acquisition of GeneSnack last year—allowing customized vitamin gummies based on 23andMe-style uploads. LatAm emphasizes affordability with VitaPack Value Bundles, fortified rice snacks at $0.99 packs, addressing 15% food inflation while hitting 20% household penetration goals in Brazil's $15 billion staples market.

Strategically, we're leaning into three megatrends: premiumization (45% of pipeline at 20-30% price premiums), sustainability (driving 15% loyalty lift per loyalty app data), and channel shift (30% of launches omnichannel, with 25% sales projected from Amazon/Instacart by FY25). This positions us to outgrow the CPG industry at 2x the rate—our guidance calls for new products to contribute 20-22% of FY24 growth.

Risks include supply chain volatility for novel ingredients like fermented pea protein, where we've locked in 80% forward contracts, and competitive intensity from private labels, now 28% of category sales per NIQ. But our 12% ROIC on new launches—versus 8% industry—gives us conviction.

Our recent marketing campaigns have resonated well with consumers, and I'd like to highlight their effectiveness, a key growth driver behind our 6% top-line growth this quarter. In the hyper-competitive CPG landscape—where we're going head-to-head with giants like Procter & Gamble, Unilever, and PepsiCo—our marketing investments aren't just line items; they're precision-engineered engines for share gain and household penetration.

We deployed $285 million in absolute advertising and promotion spend globally, flat year-over-year as a percentage of sales at 11.2%, but with a step-change in efficiency. Our overall Return on Ad Spend, or ROAS, hit 4.8x, up from 4.2x last year and ahead of our internal target of 4.5x. This was driven by a 22% increase in digital media allocation, now at 58% of total spend, versus just 42% traditional channels like linear TV and out-of-home. For context, digital ROAS clocked in at 6.7x—think programmatic video on YouTube and TikTok Shop integrations—while traditional held steady at 3.2x. These figures aren't fluff; they're validated through our proprietary marketing mix modeling using Nielsen and IRI data, cross-referenced with first-party CRM signals from our 150 million loyalty program members.

Standout campaigns that moved the needle include our Refresh Revolution platform for our flagship Refresh Beverages line—competing directly with Coke Zero and Pepsi's bubly—delivered a 28% sales lift in measured channels during the 8-week activation. We leaned into shoppable AR experiences via Snapchat lenses, partnering with 50 micro-influencers (10k-100k followers) who generated 4.2 million UGC impressions at a blended CAC of just $2.14 per new household. This drove a 15 basis points market share gain in the $28 billion non-carbonated RTD segment, per Circana data. Similarly, in snacks, the Crunch Time campaign for our Harvest Crunch bar portfolio mirrored Unilever's AXE playbook but with a health halo: 65% of ad creative emphasized 10g protein per bar, yielding 18% incremental volume in North America alone.

On the technical front, we've rolled out our AI-powered Campaign Optimizer platform, built on Google Cloud's Vertex AI and integrated with our Snowflake data lake. This crunches 2.5 petabytes of real-time signals—attribution from pixels, geolocation from mobile apps, and even weather APIs for demand forecasting. In Q3, it dynamically reallocated $120 million mid-flight from underperforming CTV slots on Hulu to high-conversion Meta Reels, boosting ROAS by 14%. We're also piloting zero-party data loops via our GCB Rewards app, where users opt-in for personalized bundles; early tests show a 3x uplift in repeat purchase rates versus broad-reach blasts.

Regionally, performance varied but trended positive across the board. In North America, our core market at 52% of sales, ROAS was 5.1x on $185 million spend, fueled by Walmart Connect and Amazon DSP dominance amid softening inflation—household penetration for our core SKUs rose 2.3 points to 68%. EMEA, at 22% of sales, faced headwinds from regulatory scrutiny on HFSS advertising (high fat, salt, sugar), but we pivoted to purpose-driven content around sustainable sourcing for our EcoClean household line, achieving 4.6x ROAS and 11% sales growth in the UK and Germany despite a 5% category contraction. APAC exploded with 7.2x ROAS on $43 million, led by China’s Douyin e-commerce lives for our K-Beauty inspired skincare—sales there surged 32% year-over-year, capturing share from L'Oréal amid premiumization trends. LatAm rounded it out at 4.1x, with Brazil's soccer-themed activations for Refresh driving 25% volume uplift during recent events.

Strategically, these results affirm our Precision Growth framework: less spray-and-pray, more data-led hyper-targeting. We're seeing clear trends—digital video now accounts for 35% of our mix, up from 22% in 2022, with attribution windows shortening to 7-day click/1-day view as consumers fragment across Roku, Prime Video, and fast commerce apps like Instacart. Sustainability messaging resonated, contributing 9% to overall lift, aligning with Nielsen's finding that 78% of global shoppers prefer eco-branded CPG. But challenges remain: rising CPMs (up 18% year-over-year on social) and iOS privacy shifts are squeezing margins, so we're doubling down on owned channels and CTV, targeting 65% digital mix by FY25.

Looking forward, we'll sustain this momentum with A&P planned for FY24 implying 5.0x+ ROAS. Key initiatives include expanding our Connected Data Organization to federate insights across retailers like Kroger and Tesco, and testing generative AI for creative variants—early pilots show 20% faster production at 15% higher engagement. We're confident this positions GCB for sustained 4-6% organic growth in a 2-3% CPG backdrop. We are also excited about the launch of our new product, VitaBloom Plant-Powered Protein Bars, which is already generating positive feedback and strong market share gains.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for questions. Our first question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs.

Emily Carter:
Good morning. Can you elaborate on the details of the new marketing campaign and its impact on sales?

Raj Singh:
Good morning, Emily. Absolutely. Our Refresh Revolution campaign for Refresh Beverages was a standout, delivering a 28% sales lift through shoppable AR on Snapchat and micro-influencer partnerships that generated millions in UGC. It drove 15 basis points of market share in non-carbonated RTDs, with ROAS at over 6x in digital channels, directly contributing to our beverages segment's 8% organic growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Lawson with JPMorgan.

Mike Lawson:
What are your plans for addressing rising commodity costs in the coming quarters?

Lisa Hargrove:
Thanks, Mike. We've got a multi-layered approach. Through CPG Agile Supply, we've locked in forward contracts for key inputs like 60% of palm oil below spot and diversified cocoa sourcing. Our $2 billion cost savings pipeline, including regenerative agriculture investments and digital twin modeling, positions us for continued margin expansion to 52-52.5% in Q4, buffering against cocoa peaks or freight disruptions.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Kim with Morgan Stanley.

Sarah Kim:
How is the current inflationary environment impacting consumer demand for your premium product lines?

Alex Rivera:
Good morning, Sarah. Inflation has prompted some downtrading, but our premium lines like Hard Seltzers, VitaBloom bars, and GlowEssence are resilient, outpacing categories with 2x growth versus value tiers. Premiumization and health & wellness trends—35% of sales now—along with targeted pricing ahead of inflation, have driven favorable mix shifts and share gains, even in softer Europe volumes.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Ruiz with Barclays.

David Ruiz:
Can you discuss the performance of your e-commerce channel this quarter?

Raj Singh:
Hi David. E-commerce was a bright spot at 22% of North America sales, up significantly, with 28% penetration growth driving 25% velocity in beverages on Amazon and Instacart. In APAC, 45% of GlowEssence sales were DTC via Tmall, fueled by live-streaming at 7x ROAS. Our omnichannel pipeline targets 25% from these platforms by FY25.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your questions and participation in today's call. Our strong gross margins, efficient A&P, category resilience, innovative launches, and effective campaigns underscore our execution. We're confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders, with FY24 organic growth of 4-6% and margin gains ahead. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Global Consumer Brands Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
